ayahOccurrences.text: ٱلَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ لَا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَقُومُ ٱلَّذِى يَتَخَبَّطُهُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ مِنَ ٱلْمَسِّ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا ٱلْبَيْعُ مِثْلُ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ ۗ وَأَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟ ۚ فَمَن جَآءَهُۥ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ فَٱنتَهَىٰ فَلَهُۥ مَا سَلَفَ وَأَمْرُهُۥٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَمَنْ عَادَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ

entries.label: عَادٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
عَادٌ ʿād [n.] an ancient Arab tribe descended from Shem, a son of Noah and ancestor of the Semites (Gen. X.21), and described as being of giant stature *

(7:74) وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ مِنْ بَعْدِ عَادٍ and remember when He made you successors after ʿād. The people of ʿād were a great tribe that dwelled in ʾal‐ʾaḥqāf (q.v.) a vast hilly desert region said to have extended between Oman and ˘aḍramawt in Arabia. Their main city ʾiram (q.v.) was described in the Qur’an

(89:7–8), as the city of lofty pillars, the like of which has never been created in the land. When their brother, the prophet Hūd, warned them against their worshipping of idols (said to have been the Goddess ʾallāt, q.v.) they called him a liar. They were punished for denying God and their mighty city was destroyed by a terrible wailing wind

(69:6) that levelled everything to the ground and left the inhabitants strewn around like felled palm trees.
